AuthenticationRequest.description: The credentials the identity provider needs: an OIDC code, or an Auth0 access token plus redirect URI

redirectURI.description: Auth0 redirect URI the code was issued against

AuthenticationResponse.description: The authenticated user's PIC-SURE token and profile

acceptedTOS.description: Whether the user accepted the latest terms of service, as the string "true"/"false"

expirationDate.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant at which the token expires

oktaIdToken.description: Okta id_token, present only for the Okta-brokered providers (AIM-AHEAD, RAS)

token.description: The PIC-SURE JWT the client sends as its bearer token

userId.description: The user's subject claim; also the session key

IntrospectionRequest.description: The token to validate plus the request being authorized

request.description: The request PSAMA is being asked to authorize

token.description: The end user's bearer token, without the Bearer prefix

LongTermTokenResponse.description: The current user's refreshed long-term token

OpenAccessValidationRequest.description: The request being authorized, plus the caller's open-access marker

request.description: The request being authorized; identical node to token introspection

TargetedRequest.description: What the gateway asks PSAMA to authorize: the request path plus, when there is one, the body being authorized. Deployed JsonPath access rules bind to this node

Target Service.description: Verbatim request path; deployed JsonPath access rules bind $.['Target Service']

query.description: The request body being authorized; bare v3 Query on query paths. Absent when the request has no body to authorize

active.description: False whenever the token is unusable for any reason: invalid, expired, unknown user, or unauthorized

email.description: Email address of the authenticated user

privileges.description: Names of the BASELINE privileges the user holds in the calling application, plus their application-independent ones. PSAMA no longer mints per-study PRIV_MANAGED_* privileges or FENCE-derived names at login, so nothing here describes which studies the user may query: study access flows exclusively through user_consents, read via GET /user/me/consents.

query.description: Consent-mutated v3 Query as a JSON OBJECT (never a string). Present only when access-rule evaluation rewrote the submitted query; the caller must run this one instead of the query it sent

roles.description: Names of the BASELINE roles held by the user. PSAMA no longer mints per-study MANAGED_* roles or FENCE-derived role names at login, so nothing here describes which studies the user may query: study access flows exclusively through user_consents, read via GET /user/me/consents.

sub.description: Token subject, i.e. the identity-provider-scoped user identifier

token.description: The refreshed token; populated only when tokenRefreshed is true

tokenRefreshed.description: True when PSAMA issued a fresh token because the presented one was close to expiring

userId.description: PSAMA's UUID for the authenticated user

TokenRefreshResponse.description: A refreshed PIC-SURE token and its expiry

expirationDate.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant at which the token expires

UserConsentsResponse.description: The study authorizations of the caller, keyed by concept path

consents.description: Authorized consent identifiers, keyed by CONCEPT PATH -- not by study accession. The values are the consent identifiers verbatim ("phs000007.c1", "open_access-1000Genomes"); clients match them against dictionary values and put them in a v3 query's authorizationFilters as-is, never parsing or reformatting them. The producer is PSAMA's BdcConsentsBuilder, and the keys it writes today are "\_consents\" (every authorized consent identifier plus every public study), "\_harmonized_consent\" (the harmonized subset) and "\_topmed_consents\" (the subset whose study dataType contains G). Those are the KNOWN keys, not the complete set: consumers must treat every key as optional and tolerate ones they do not recognise. Empty when nothing is authorized.

userId.description: PSAMA's UUID for the user these consents belong to

ValidationResponse.description: Whether the open-access request passed the open-access rule set

valid.description: true when the request is authorized
